subject: problems with plotting and accessing intensities

messages.author: 1e9533b2bf521f06
messages.subject: problems with plotting and accessing intensities
parts:
Hello,

I loaded 22 SNP 6.0 array files and now have a object called cs.
AffymetrixCelSet:
Name: group1
Tags: testSet
Path: rawData/group1,testSet/GenomeWideSNP_6
Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full
Number of arrays: 22
Names: A1, A10, ..., C9
Time period: 2007-11-30 11:40:13 -- 2007-12-03 16:43:30
Total file size: 1449.10MB
RAM: 0.02MB

I want to do the following:
1.plot a principal component analysis of the samples (plot.prcomp?).
How do I do this?
2.plotDensity. for this i tried doing
plotDensity(cs)
Error in apply.default(mat, 2, density) :
dim(X) must have a positive length

3. Look at the intensities of individual arrays. For this i tried
cs[[1]], but i got the following error:
Error in readCelUnits(pathnames, cdf = cdf, ...) :
No CDF file for chip type found: GenomeWideSNP_6

thanks
manisha

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] problems with plotting and accessing intensities
parts:
On Tue, Sep 16, 2008 at 10:13 AM, biobee <manis...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> I loaded 22 SNP 6.0 array files and now have a object called cs.
> AffymetrixCelSet:
> Name: group1
> Tags: testSet
> Path: rawData/group1,testSet/GenomeWideSNP_6
> Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full
> Number of arrays: 22
> Names: A1, A10, ..., C9
> Time period: 2007-11-30 11:40:13 -- 2007-12-03 16:43:30
> Total file size: 1449.10MB
> RAM: 0.02MB

>
> I want to do the following:
> 1.plot a principal component analysis of the samples (plot.prcomp?).
> How do I do this?

There is nothing in aroma.affymetrix implemented for this. Your
question is quite generic, because you do not say what you kind of
signals or estimates you want to use to do PCA on.

> 2.plotDensity. for this i tried doing
> plotDensity(cs)
> Error in apply.default(mat, 2, density) :
> dim(X) must have a positive length

This is a known issue (see thread 'problem in plotDensity' on August
26, 2008). As explained there, the solution is to make sure to load
the 'affy' package *before* loading 'aroma.affymetrix', i.e.

library(affy);
library(aroma.affymetrix);

This will be automatically solved in the next release.

>
> 3. Look at the intensities of individual arrays. For this i tried
> cs[[1]], but i got the following error:
> Error in readCelUnits(pathnames, cdf = cdf, ...) :
> No CDF file for chip type found: GenomeWideSNP_6

If you care about the structure of probes according to the CDF, use:

> y <- readUnits(csR, units=102:103)
> str(y);
List of 2
$ SNP_A-1683663:List of 4
..$ C:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:10, 1:10] 728 1917 952 1881 964 ...
..$ T:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:10, 1:10] 1759 3925 2042 3265 966 ...
..$ C:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:10, 1:10] 704 635 926 729 930 ...
..$ T:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:10, 1:10] 1300 2274 2431 598 2292 ...
$ SNP_A-1739552:List of 4
..$ C:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:8, 1:10] 1276 518 1537 520 1893 ...
..$ T:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:8, 1:10] 5694 1117 5194 1019 2964 ...
..$ C:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:12, 1:10] 399 785 854 1410 884 ...
..$ T:List of 1
.. ..$ intensities: num [1:12, 1:10] 1024 4091 1425 4338 3600 ...

If you only want to access the probe values by their intensities, use
extractMatrix(), e.g.

> y <- extractMatrix(csR, cells=1:100);
> str(y)
num [1:100, 1:10] 1369 65472 1874 65477 725 ...
- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
..$ : NULL
..$ : chr [1:10] "NA06985" "NA06991" "NA06993" "NA06994" ...

BTW, from where did you find out about using [[ ]] like that? If it
is documented somewhere, I will remove/correct it (it was indeed a
valid feature in one of "alpha-alpha" versions).

Hope this helps

Henrik

PS. Next time you post, please only bring up one kind of topic per
message, that is, it is better to post one message per topic. DS.

>
> thanks
> manisha
>
> >
>
